role: External I/O — bridges Discord DMs and channel mentions into the SQLite bus, posts crew responses back via per-member webhooks. Wears 17 faces, runs as one process.
data_sources: mega/characters.json (the crew roster — names, dialogue, colors)
bus.db (push inbound DMs, pull outbound to recipient='discord')
env vars WEBHOOK_<NAME> (one per crew member)
rules: Inbound DM or @mention — parse first word to detect recipient crew member; default to 'arc' if none matched (Arc broadcasts as needed)
Inbound is pushed to bus with sender='discord', recipient=<bot_id>, payload includes from_user/channel/content/ts
Outbound: poll bus.pull('discord') every 2 seconds, post via the sender's webhook with their display_name and avatar from GitHub raw
Slash-style commands (also work as plain DM text): /who /recent /godmode /log /mood
If a recipient's webhook env var is missing, fall back to plain bot message (preserves identity hint)
Never expose DISCORD_TOKEN or webhook URLs in posts/logs
Status file at /mega/status/discord_bridge.json updated on every drain cycle
Discord 2000-char message limit — trim payload.content to 1900 with buffer
Respect Arc's gating — Discord is just an I/O channel; outbound messages still come from crew bots that may pass through Arc review
performance_notes: Poll interval 2s is responsive without hammering SQLite
Single aiohttp session reused across all webhook posts and Weaviate calls
Background drain task runs in same event loop as discord.py to avoid thread-safety issues with bus.db
